items.value: Dust is indeed more concentrated over subtropical and temperate areas, but the reason is that these areas have MORE dry winds, not less
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: dust concentration is highest over subtropical and temperate regions and lower over equatorial and polar regions. Statement II inverts the cause. Dust is lifted and held aloft by dry, turbulent winds, so it is precisely because subtropical and temperate belts experience abundant dry winds (and little washout by rain) that they carry more dust; equatorial regions have heavy convectional rainfall that scavenges dust from the air, and polar regions have little loose surface material. Saying these areas have 'less dry winds' contradicts the very mechanism that produces Statement I.

items.value: Both are correct, and the warmer January ocean air is exactly why isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over land
items.reasoning: January is Northern Hemisphere winter. Land has a low specific heat and cools quickly, while the ocean retains summer heat, so at any given latitude the sea is warmer than the continent. A line of equal temperature must therefore run further south (equatorward) to find that temperature over land, and further north (poleward) to find it over the sea, which is exactly Statement I. Statement II states this land-sea thermal contrast, so it is not merely true alongside Statement I but is its cause, making A correct rather than B.

items.value: Statement II alone is correct and explains Statement I; Statement III is false because clay is in fact highly porous, just not permeable
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: chalk is a permeable rock and clay is effectively impermeable. Statement II is correct and is the explanation for the chalk half of Statement I, since chalk's open pore network lets it take in and transmit water. Statement III is the trap and is false: clay has very high porosity, often 40 to 60 per cent void space, but its pores are microscopic and poorly connected, so water cannot pass through. Porosity and permeability are different properties, and clay is the standard illustration of a rock that is porous yet impermeable. With III false and II true and explanatory, only option C fits.

items.value: All three greenhouse-effect statements are correct
items.reasoning: Statement II is correct: it is the heat absorbed and re-radiated by the atmosphere that holds Earth's average surface temperature near 15 degrees Celsius. Statement III is correct: carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane absorb outgoing longwave radiation strongly, which is what makes them greenhouse gases. Statement I states the standard consequence, that without this blanketing the surface would fall far below freezing, the usual figure quoted being about minus 18 degrees Celsius. The word 'everywhere' is loose, since an airless Earth would also lose the atmosphere's heat redistribution and its sunlit face could be hot, but the claim is the one made in the standard textbook treatment and is intended as correct here.

items.value: Both statements about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission are correct
items.reasoning: Statement II states the Mission's founding purpose accurately: launched in December 2014, the Rashtriya Gokul Mission is aimed at development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds through scientific and holistic breeding and rearing. Statement I states the official rationale for its pro-poor character, namely that most low-yielding indigenous animals are held by small and marginal farmers and landless labourers, so raising their productivity directly raises rural incomes. Both are correct, so C.

items.value: Both II and III are correct, but only III, the calcination of limestone to lime, explains cement's large share of global CO2
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct, since cement accounts for roughly 7 to 8 per cent of global CO2, comfortably more than 5 per cent. Statement II is correct as a description of the raw mix, as silica-bearing clay or shale is blended with limestone. Statement III is correct and is the actual reason for the emissions: in the kiln, calcium carbonate decomposes to calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, and this calcination releases CO2 from the rock itself, contributing more than half of cement's footprint before any fuel is burnt. Merely mixing clay with limestone releases no CO2, so II does not explain I and the answer is B, not A.

items.value: Only Statement III is correct, and the concern about health-system resilience is why India did not sign; the Declaration is not binding
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: India did not join the COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health. Statement II is false, because COP declarations of this kind are political and voluntary, carrying no legal obligation to decarbonise any sector. Statement III reflects the reason India actually gave, that commitments to cut emissions from health facilities could constrain the cooling, refrigeration and power-intensive infrastructure on which the resilience of its health-care system depends. So exactly one of the two supporting statements is correct and it does explain Statement I, which is option C.

items.value: Both II and III are true statements, but only the equatorward migration of meltwater explains the shift in Earth's rotation and axis
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct, as studies of polar motion show the rotation axis drifting and the length of day changing. Statement III is correct and is the mechanism: melting polar ice moves mass from high latitudes towards the equator, altering Earth's moment of inertia and shifting the pole. Statement II is also a true statement in itself, since flares and coronal mass ejections do deposit enormous energy in the thermosphere, but that energy acts on a thin outer gas layer and does not redistribute the planet's mass or move its spin axis. Two correct statements with only one explanatory gives B.

items.value: Both II and III correctly describe Article 6 and both are why it is so heavily discussed
items.reasoning: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement has two limbs and both statements name one of them. Article 6.2 and 6.4 establish cooperative approaches and a centralised crediting mechanism, that is the architecture of international carbon markets, so Statement II is correct. Article 6.8 establishes a framework for non-market approaches between countries, phrased in the Agreement itself as being in the context of sustainable development and poverty eradication, so Statement III is correct. Both limbs are precisely what makes Article 6 the most negotiated and most discussed provision in climate and sustainable-development forums, so both explain Statement I.

items.value: The Asian Development Bank launched the Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific
items.reasoning: The Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific was launched by the Asian Development Bank, announced at COP28, to mobilise finance for nature-based solutions across its developing member countries. The name itself carries ADB's signature regional formulation 'Asia and the Pacific', which is how ADB frames its mandate; AIIB is infrastructure-focused, the New Development Bank is the BRICS bank with no Asia-Pacific regional remit, and the IBRD is the World Bank's global arm.

items.value: All three uses of Direct Air Capture are correct: sequestration, industrial and food uses, and synthetic aviation fuel
items.reasoning: Direct Air Capture extracts CO2 from ambient air, and what happens next defines its uses. Statement I is correct because the captured CO2 can be injected into geological formations for permanent storage, which is carbon sequestration and is the main climate rationale for the technology. Statement II is correct because captured CO2 is a feedstock for polymers and plastics and is used in food and beverage processing, for example carbonation and chilling. Statement III is correct because CO2 combined with low-carbon hydrogen yields synthetic hydrocarbon e-fuels, the leading route to low-carbon aviation fuel that does not depend on biomass.

items.value: Only II and III are correct; the Peacock tarantula is an arachnid, not an omnivorous crustacean
items.reasoning: Statement I is false on two counts: the Gooty or Peacock tarantula, Poecilotheria metallica, is a spider and therefore an arachnid, not a crustacean, and it is a predator feeding on insects and other small animals rather than an omnivore. Statement II is correct, as the species is endemic to a very small patch of reserve forest in Andhra Pradesh and is listed Critically Endangered precisely because of that tiny range. Statement III is correct, since Poecilotheria are arboreal, sheltering in holes and crevices of tall trees rather than in ground burrows.

items.value: Only II and III are correct; India's per-capita CO2 is around 2 tonnes, far above the 0.5 tonne claimed
items.reasoning: Statement I is false by a wide margin: India emits roughly 2.5 to 2.9 gigatonnes of energy-related CO2 for a population of about 1.4 billion, giving close to 2 tonnes per capita, about four times the 0.5 tonne figure in the statement. Statement II is correct, as India is second only to China for CO2 from fuel combustion in the Asia-Pacific region. Statement III is correct, since electricity and heat generation, dominated by coal, is by a large margin India's biggest emitting sector, ahead of industry and transport.

items.value: Three pairs are correctly matched: cassava, ginger and Malabar spinach; mint and papaya are wrong
items.reasoning: Cassava, Manihot esculenta, is a perennial woody shrub one to three metres tall, so I is correct. Ginger is a herbaceous perennial whose aerial shoot is a pseudostem formed of rolled leaf sheaths, so II is correct. Malabar spinach, Basella alba, is a succulent herbaceous twining climber, so III is correct. Mint is a perennial herb, not an annual shrub, so IV is wrong on both the life-span and the habit. Papaya is an unbranched, soft-stemmed short-lived plant usually classed as a giant herb or herbaceous tree, not a woody shrub, so V is wrong. That leaves three correct pairs.

items.value: Only statement II is correct: marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria supply about half the world's oxygen
items.reasoning: Statement II is correct and is the accepted figure, with marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria such as Prochlorococcus producing at least half of atmospheric oxygen. Statement I is therefore false, since it reverses the comparison: the ocean out-produces the rainforests, and mature rainforests in any case consume through respiration and decay nearly as much oxygen as they generate. Statement III is false and inverted: air is about 21 per cent oxygen, equivalent to roughly 300 milligrams per litre, whereas even well-oxygenated surface water carries only about 8 to 10 milligrams per litre, so water holds many times less oxygen than air, not more.

items.value: All three are alternative powertrain vehicles
items.reasoning: An alternative powertrain is any drivetrain that replaces the conventional internal combustion engine running on petrol or diesel. A full battery electric vehicle drives on stored electricity, a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle generates its electricity on board from hydrogen, and a fuel cell-electric hybrid combines a fuel cell with a battery. None uses a conventional combustion powertrain, so all three qualify.

items.value: None of the statements is correct, because each says 'all types' of UAV and fixed-wing UAVs break every one
items.reasoning: Each statement is a universal claim about all UAVs, so a single class of exception falsifies it, and fixed-wing UAVs are that exception throughout. Statement I fails because conventional fixed-wing drones land on a runway or are recovered by net, parachute or arrester, not vertically. Statement II fails because a fixed-wing aircraft must maintain forward airspeed to generate lift and cannot hover at all, automatically or otherwise. Statement III fails because many UAVs, especially larger military and long-endurance types, run on internal combustion or turbine engines, and others use solar or hybrid power, so battery is not the only source.

items.value: Three of them, cobalt, lithium and nickel, are cathode materials; graphite is the anode
items.reasoning: In a lithium-ion cell the cathode is a lithium metal oxide, most commonly nickel-manganese-cobalt or nickel-cobalt-aluminium chemistry, so lithium, cobalt and nickel are all cathode constituents. Graphite is the standard anode material, into whose layers lithium ions intercalate during charging, and it is not part of the cathode. That gives three of the four listed elements.

items.value: All three contain plastic
items.reasoning: Cigarette butts contain plastic because the filter is made of cellulose acetate, a synthetic polymer, which is why butts are among the most abundant plastic items collected in litter surveys. Most modern eyeglass lenses are plastic polymers such as CR-39 or polycarbonate, which have largely displaced glass. Car tyres are built from synthetic rubber, itself a petroleum-derived polymer, and tyre wear is one of the largest sources of microplastic released into the environment. So all three qualify.

items.value: All three can be produced using coal gasification, though the nitroglycerine link runs indirectly through ammonia and nitric acid
items.reasoning: Coal gasification yields syngas, a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen that is a versatile chemical feedstock. Ethanol is produced from syngas by catalytic or fermentation routes, and coal-to-ethanol is an announced Indian project, so I holds. Urea is the clearest case, since syngas hydrogen makes ammonia and ammonia plus CO2 makes urea, so III holds. Nitroglycerine is the doubtful one: it is nitrated glycerol, and the connection to coal is only through the nitric acid, which is made from coal-derived ammonia, a route also used for coal-based ammonium nitrate explosives in mining. Because that link is indirect rather than a direct product of gasification, the intended answer could equally be 'only two', and this item should be treated as unsettled.

items.value: CL-20, HMX and LLM-105 are all military high explosives
items.reasoning: All three are nitrogen-rich energetic organic compounds developed as high explosives. HMX, or octogen, is a long-established military high explosive; CL-20 is a more powerful caged nitramine developed as its successor; and LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive designed to resist accidental detonation. Options C and D are the near-misses, because HMX and CL-20 do also appear as ingredients in solid rocket propellant formulations, but LLM-105 is purely an insensitive explosive and is not a propellant fuel, so the characteristic common to all three is that they are explosives, not fuels. Option A is unrelated, as none is a refrigerant.

items.value: I and III are correct; Majorana 1 is Microsoft's chip, not AWS's
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct, as the Majorana 1 chip is a quantum processor built on a topological architecture and is intended to make scalable quantum computing possible. Statement II is false, because Majorana 1 was announced by Microsoft in February 2025; Amazon Web Services announced a separate quantum chip called Ocelot. Statement III is correct, since deep learning, which uses multi-layered neural networks, is a subset of machine learning, which is itself a subset of artificial intelligence.

items.value: All three statements about monoclonal antibodies are correct
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: monoclonal antibodies are antibodies, which are proteins, produced in the laboratory from a single clone of cells rather than arising naturally in the patient. Statement II is correct in the sense intended, since a monoclonal antibody binds one specific antigen and thereby marks the target for the immune system, recruiting effector mechanisms such as antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity and complement activation. Statement III is correct: the monoclonal antibody m102.4 has been used against Nipah virus, including doses procured by India during Kerala outbreaks, and monoclonals were widely used against COVID-19.

items.value: None of the three statements is correct; each is a false universal negative
items.reasoning: Statement I is false, as marine viruses are the most abundant biological entities in the ocean, present at around ten million particles per millilitre of seawater. Statement II is false, since bacteriophages are viruses whose entire life cycle depends on infecting bacteria. Statement III is false, because altering host gene expression is central to how viruses replicate, with many viral proteins directly hijacking or shutting down host transcription. All three are sweeping 'no virus can' claims and each is contradicted by basic virology, so none is correct.

items.value: Both II and III are correct, and together they explain why activated carbon is both a good and an attractive remediation tool
items.reasoning: Statement I makes two claims, that activated carbon is 'good' and that it is 'attractive', and each supporting statement answers one of them. Statement II is correct and explains why it is good: an enormous internal surface area, often above a thousand square metres per gram, gives it a high adsorption capacity for heavy metals and organic pollutants. Statement III is correct and explains why it is attractive: it can be prepared cheaply from carbon-rich wastes such as coconut shell, rice husk and other agricultural residues, which keeps costs low and turns a waste stream into a product. Since both supporting statements bear on Statement I, the answer is A rather than B.
